The '''Chiha no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' ({{lang|ja|千葉国造}}, also read ''Chiha kokuzō'') were the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|lt=kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=国造}} who governed [[#Territory|Chiha Province]].

== Overview ==
=== Clan ===
The '''{{ill|Ōkisaibe clan|ja|大私部氏|lt=Ōkisaibe clan|lt_ja=大私部氏}}''' (おおきさいべうじ), with the {{ill|Kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} {{ill|Atai|ja|直 (姓)|lt=atai|lt_ja=直}}.

The right-capital imperial-branch section of the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku|lt_ja=新撰姓氏録}}'' says: "Ōkisaibe: descendants of {{ill|Hikoimasu no Miko|ja|彦坐命|lt=Hikoimasu|lt_ja=彦坐命}}, son of Emperor Kaika." Iida Takesato explained that the character 私 is read ''kisai'' because, in the commentary of Fu Qian on the biography of Zhang Fang in the ''Book of Han'', 私官 is glossed as the office of the empress, and the ''Book of the Later Han'' also has a "director of the private treasury of the middle palace"; the use of 私 for the empress follows Chinese precedent. ''Kisaibe'' is a sound change of the older, more correct ''kisakibe''. He held that the name Ōkisaibe was given to a group established for an empress before the reign of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|lt=Emperor Bidatsu|lt_ja=敏達天皇}}, distinct from the ''kisaibe'' established in Bidatsu's reign.<ref>Iida Takesato, ''Nihon Shoki Tsūshaku'' (1899).</ref> It is thus recorded as a {{ill|Tomobe|ja|伴部|lt=tomobe|lt_ja=伴部}} established for an empress dowager before the sixth century, and like the {{ill|Kisaibe|ja|私部|lt=kisaibe|lt_ja=私部}}, {{ill|Minashirobe|ja|御名代部|lt=minashirobe|lt_ja=御名代部}}, {{ill|Mikoshirobe|ja|御子代部|lt=mikoshirobe|lt_ja=御子代部}} and {{ill|Himatsuribe|ja|日奉部|lt=himatsuribe|lt_ja=日祀部}}, it was a {{ill|Bemin|ja|部民|lt=be|lt_ja=部民}} directly under the imperial house.<ref name="#1">Chiba City History Compilation Council, ''Chiba-shi Shi'' (Chiba City, 1974).</ref><ref name="#2">https://adeac.jp/chiba-city/text-list/d100010/ht002370</ref>

=== History ===
When the Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was established is recorded neither in the ''{{ill|Kiki|ja|記紀|lt=Kiki|lt_ja=記紀}}'' nor in the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi|lt_ja=先代旧事本紀}}''. The name "Ōkisaibe no Atai Yoshihito, Chiha no Kuni no Miyatsuko" appears only in the ''Nihon Kōki'', in the entries for Enryaku 24 (805) and the following Daidō 1 (806). Yoshihito received Outer Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, at the beginning of the Heian period, 161 years after the {{ill|Taika Reform|ja|大化改新|lt=Taika Reform|lt_ja=大化改新}}, by which time the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' system had already been abolished: {{ill|Kokushi|ja|国司|lt=provincial governors|lt_ja=国司}} were sent out from the centre, most local clans were appointed {{ill|Gunji|ja|郡司|lt=district officials|lt_ja=郡司}} or lower, and the centralised ''ritsuryō'' state was fully established. Views therefore divide between the opinion that the Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' "did not exist in the process by which the 'Kokuzō Hongi' was formed, and was a so-called ''ritsuryō kuni no miyatsuko'' appointed after the ''ritsuryō'' system came into force", and the opinion that "the pre-reform Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was officially allowed to keep the title after the reform, and inherited the ''atai'' rank befitting its lineage".<ref name="#1"/><ref name="#2"/>

On the first view, before the reform the Bōsō peninsula was called the land of Fusa, whose northern half held the {{ill|Inba kuni no miyatsuko|ja|印波国造|lt=Inba kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=印波国造}}, based around {{ill|Lake Inba|ja|印旛沼|lt=Lake Inba|lt_ja=印旛沼}}, and the {{ill|Shimotsu Unakami kuni no miyatsuko|ja|下海上国造|lt=Shimotsu Unakami kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=下海上国造}}, ruling the lower reaches of the present {{ill|Tone River|ja|利根川|lt=Tone River|lt_ja=利根川}}. Under the post-reform administrative divisions this became {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|lt=Shimōsa Province|lt_ja=下総国}}. The Inba territory was divided into the eight districts later recorded in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|lt=Engishiki|lt_ja=延喜式}}'' and the ''{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|ja|和名抄|lt=Wamyōshō|lt_ja=和名抄}}'', {{ill|Inba District|ja|印旛郡|lt=Inba|lt_ja=印旛郡}}, {{ill|Hanyū District, Chiba|ja|埴生郡|lt=Hanyū|lt_ja=埴生郡}}, {{ill|Chiba District|ja|千葉郡|lt=Chiba|lt_ja=千葉郡}}, {{ill|Katsushika District|ja|葛飾郡|lt=Katsushika|lt_ja=葛飾郡}}, {{ill|Sōma District, Chiba|ja|相馬郡|lt=Sōma|lt_ja=相馬郡}}, {{ill|Sashima District|ja|猿島郡|lt=Sashima|lt_ja=猿島郡}}, {{ill|Yūki District|ja|結城郡|lt=Yūki|lt_ja=結城郡}} and {{ill|Okada District|ja|岡田郡|lt=Okada|lt_ja=岡田郡}}, and the Shimotsu Unakami territory into the three districts of {{ill|Unakami District, Chiba|ja|海上郡|lt=Unakami|lt_ja=海上郡}}, {{ill|Sōsa District|ja|匝瑳郡|lt=Sōsa|lt_ja=匝瑳郡}} and {{ill|Katori District|ja|香取郡|lt=Katori|lt_ja=香取郡}}. The descendants of the Inba ''kuni no miyatsuko'' were appointed district officials of Inba, those of the Shimotsu Unakami of Unakami, and the Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was chosen from the newly created Chiba District. The names "Hasetsukabe no Atai Ushikai, Outer Senior Sixth Rank Upper, Senior Governor of Inba District, Shimōsa Province" in the ''{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|lt=Shoku Nihongi|lt_ja=続日本紀}}'' for {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応 (日本)|lt=Ten'ō|lt_ja=天応}} 1 (781), "Hasetsukabe no Atai Ōmaro of Inba District" in book 20 of the ''{{ill|Man'yōshū|ja|万葉集|lt=Man'yōshū|lt_ja=万葉集}}'', "Osada no Himatsuri no Atai Haruoka, Outer Senior Sixth Rank Upper, Senior Governor of Unakami District, Unakami no Kuni no Miyatsuko" in the ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|lt_ja=日本三代実録}}'' for the 19th day of the third month of {{ill|Ninna|ja|仁和|lt=Ninna|lt_ja=仁和}} 1 (885), and "Osada no Himatsuri no Atai Okotari, Unakami no Kuni no Miyatsuko, of Unakami District" in book 20 of the ''Man'yōshū'' are thought to be people of such lineages.<ref name="#1"/><ref name="#2"/>

However, it is more reasonable to see the pre-Taika title of ''kuni no miyatsuko'', as in "Osada no Himatsuri no Atai Haruoka" and "Okotari" above, "Izumo no Omi Hiroshima, Outer Junior Seventh Rank Lower, Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko" in the ''Shoku Nihongi'' for the first month of {{ill|Jinki (era)|ja|神亀|lt=Jinki|lt_ja=神亀}} 1, and "Kusakabe no Atai Masuhito, Izu no Kuni no Miyatsuko" for the fourth month of {{ill|Tenpyō|ja|天平|lt=Tenpyō|lt_ja=天平}} 14, as granted together with a ''kabane'' to the old ''kuni no miyatsuko'' families who presided over {{ill|Shinji|ja|神事|lt=rites|lt_ja=神事}} and {{ill|Saishi|ja|祭祀|lt=worship|lt_ja=祭祀}} even after the system was abolished. That makes a pre-Taika Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' possible, and since the Inba and Shimotsu Unakami ''kuni no miyatsuko'' were appointed in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ōjin|lt_ja=応神天皇}}, the Chiha appointment can be placed in about the same period, when the powerful clans of the northern Bōsō peninsula came one after another under the Yamato court, and the strongest chiefs among them were made ''kuni no miyatsuko''.<ref name="#1"/><ref name="#2"/> On this view, the Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' submitted anew to the Yamato kingship at a time not much earlier than the reign of Emperor Bidatsu, like the Inba and Kamitsu Unakami ''kuni no miyatsuko'' (late sixth century) and the {{ill|Ijimu kuni no miyatsuko|ja|伊甚国造|lt=Ijimu kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=伊甚国造}} (early sixth century).<ref name="#1"/><ref name="#2"/>

== Base ==
=== Territory ===
The territory of the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was the region called '''Chiha Province''', later {{ill|Chiba District|ja|千葉郡|lt=Chiba District|lt_ja=千葉郡}} of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ja|下総国|lt=Shimōsa Province|lt_ja=下総国}}, corresponding to present-day {{ill|Chiba (city)|ja|千葉市|lt=Chiba city|lt_ja=千葉市}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|lt=Chiba Prefecture|lt_ja=千葉県}}.

It is not mentioned in the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''Sendai Kuji Hongi'', but the ''{{ill|Nihon Kōki|ja|日本後紀|lt=Nihon Kōki|lt_ja=日本後紀}}'' records under the 8th day of the tenth month of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|lt=Enryaku|lt_ja=延暦}} 24 (805) that the Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' {{ill|Ōkisaibe no Atai Yoshihito|ja|大私部直善人|lt=Ōkisaibe no Atai Yoshihito|lt_ja=大私部直善人}} was granted {{ill|Ge'i|ja|外位|lt=Outer|lt_ja=外}} {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位下|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade|lt_ja=従五位下}}, and under the 28th day of the first month of the following Daidō 1 (806) that he was appointed {{ill|Jō (official)|ja|大掾|lt=senior secretary|lt_ja=大掾}} of Shimōsa Province. The name of the Chiha ''kuni no miyatsuko'' appears nowhere but the ''Nihon Kōki''.

The name Chiha is explained either as meaning "many leaves growing thick", because the area was a {{ill|Wilderness|ja|原野|lt=wild plain|lt_ja=原野}} overgrown with {{ill|Plant|ja|草木|lt=plants and trees|lt_ja=草木}}, or as expressing a wish for the prosperity of the {{ill|Land|ja|土地|lt=land|lt_ja=土地}}.

== People ==
* '''Ōkisaibe no Yoshihito''' (おおきさいべのよしひと)
*: A ''kuni no miyatsuko'' of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|lt=Heian period|lt_ja=平安時代}}, senior secretary of Shimōsa Province.

== Clan deity ==
Unknown.
